analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE workflow lines 1–1230 and the bounded patch. The visible addition at .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml HEAD 64–76 disables Actions caching on darkbloom-* runners lacking DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL; it does not visibly introduce credential use or change runtime authorization, encryption, billing, or prompt handling. Updated comments describe size-off routing to an approval-pinned macOS size rather than Blacksmith, but the route implementation is not supplied.
BASE controls include read-only permissions, SHA-pinned external actions, checkout without persisted credentials, push/dispatch-only cache saves (lines 28–39), strict-cache forwarding (119,198), blocking native/media gates (420–500), suite-plan auditing (523–533), and a fail-closed selected-lane gate (1151–1198). Existing nonblocking GPU tests and cached .git behavior are not new findings. CI artifact/cache integrity is relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054; native test coverage also supports TB-007, T-050 and T-041. Test-only prefix-cache disabling at BASE 461–472 does not change production cache policy.
No concrete regression is established by the supplied patch. However, HEAD bodies for the numerous cache-condition, .git-validation and GPU-runner changes are absent; changed-range metadata cannot establish their semantics. Integration must compare the complete HEAD workflow with this BASE, inspect provider-plan.yml routing/approval handling and the cache endpoint contract, and confirm cache-disabled jobs still build/test correctly and that untrusted PR jobs cannot contaminate trusted build caches or artifact qualification. This is a material coverage limit, not evidence those controls are missing.
